column7: TRIGGER-HARDEN-1 (follow-up of docs/design/trigger-rowdigest.md). The per-read proof checks only that the secret_nodes cache-epoch trigger exists and is ENABLE ALWAYS, so the owner of its function (the server database role, no superuser needed) could replace the body with one that stamps nothing, ALTER FUNCTION ... SET search_path, or re-create the trigger as AFTER or with a WHEN clause, and a direct update then left cache_epoch unchanged while every warm replica kept serving the old row. The periodic check (secret_node_cache_epoch_integrity.go, run by the same job as the role-permission check) compares the function body, language, exact proconfig and security mode and the trigger definition with this release and the catalog rows xmin with the last reading; on a difference it logs, counts keyorix_secret_node_cache_epoch_tamper_total, bumps cache_epoch of every secret_nodes row, re-installs and bumps again. Also _AlteredSearchPathIsRestored_Postgres, _SecurityDefinerIsRestored_Postgres, _DisableWriteEnableInOneTransactionIsFlushed_Postgres, _ReplaceThenRestoreIsFlushed_Postgres, _TriggerRecreatedAfterOrWithWhenIsRestored_Postgres, _FailedRepairIsRetriedNotAdopted_Postgres, _CleanTicksAndReplicaBootsDoNotFlush_Postgres, _BackgroundJobFlushesAndStopsOnClose_Postgres; installer half TestSecretNodeCacheEpoch_EnsureLeavesCorrectFunctionRowAlone_Postgres and _EnsureRestoresRecreatedTrigger_Postgres (both red on main by behaviour). The search_path pin itself landed in #3631 (TestSecretNodeCacheEpoch_WriterSearchPathCannotShadowTheBump_Postgres). Residual: one interval for deliberate DDL; a superuser below SQL is not detected; the cache_epoch column is not covered.
